title: Benchmark Report (Latency/$) — Kickoff Notes (Working Doc)
content:
Doc purpose (working):
Capture kickoff decisions + open questions for the public Benchmark Report focused on production inference economics (latency/$). This will feed the report outline, landing page copy, and enablement kit.

Meeting info
- Date: 2025-06-03
- Channel: #marketing / cross-functional working session
- Notes owner: Soojin Lee (PMM)

Attendees (core)
- PMM/Launch: Soojin Lee
- Content: Ethan Wallace
- Benchmark leads: Jonas Weber, Claire Dubois, Rina Kobayashi
- Eng partners: Vanessa Ortiz (Fleet/Capacity), Neha Kapoor (Reliability)
- Product: Henry Cho
- Growth: Ben Carter
- Web: Felix Schneider, Alicia Perez
- Legal: Michael Grant, Sofia Mendes
- Sales/SE: Markus Klein (enablement)

1) What we are shipping (scope + outputs)
Primary outputs (launch package)
- Public landing page with interactive table (filterable by model/region/context length; metric toggles)
- Downloadable PDF benchmark report (with methodology section + caveats)
- Blog post (narrative + key takeaways + how to reproduce at high level)
- Sales enablement kit (talk track, FAQ/objection handling, 1-slide/1-pager)

Primary goal
- Be the most credible source for production inference economics: show latency + cost together, not just raw tokens/sec.
- Drive top-of-funnel (self-serve signups) and sales-assisted pipeline (Dedicated/Private), without overclaiming.

Success metrics (initial)
- Marketing funnel: benchmark page traffic, time on page, interactive engagement (filter/export/CTA), signups, activation, demo requests
- Sales: MQL->SQL, influenced pipeline tagged to campaign, # of benchmark-sourced meetings
- Trust/credibility: low rate of “fairness” pushback, ability to point to a defensible methodology + retained artifacts

Non-goals / guardrails
- Not an ongoing “forever benchmark program” for v1 (we’ll define a short post-launch maintenance window)
- No product changes solely for benchmark optics (small telemetry/guardrail changes OK)
- Avoid “best/fastest/cheapest” blanket claims; avoid implying competitor malfeasance

2) Audience and positioning (draft)
Primary audience
- Engineers + ML engineers building LLM apps who care about: p95 latency, throughput under concurrency, predictable cost
Secondary
- Platform/security teams: deployment flexibility (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), data residency/regions, auditability

Core message (draft)
- “Latency/$ is the metric that matches production reality. Redwood makes inference more predictable and economical across regions and workloads.”

Key proof points we expect to lean on (pending data)
- Strong latency/$ for popular open models under realistic prefill/decode mixes
- Regional consistency (smaller deltas between NA/EU/APAC than folks expect)
- Stability / low variance with transparent methodology (reruns when variance exceeds threshold)

3) Metric + methodology highlights (early alignment)
Metric we will publish (working definition)
- Latency/$: normalized “milliseconds per generated token per dollar” (or equivalent), with supporting metrics:
  - p50/p95 end-to-end latency
  - throughput (tokens/sec) at defined concurrency
  - $/1M tokens (prefill and decode breakout where possible)

Workload realism principles (agreement in room)
- Must represent production mixes: not only long-form decode; include prefill-heavy requests
- Must define caching/batching policy explicitly; no hidden “special sauce” that customers can’t access
- Use repeated runs + stability gates; publish ranges/notes where variance exists

Open methodology questions (need owners + deadlines)
- Caching policy: enabled by default or off? If enabled, what % cache hit assumption is fair?
  - Working direction: publish two modes if feasible:
    1) “Cold” (cache disabled / cleared between runs)
    2) “Warm prefix” (documented prefix cache behavior) — only if we can make it reproducible and not misleading
- Streaming vs non-streaming: do we publish streaming-specific metrics or keep it simple?
  - Working direction: keep headline metric non-streaming; include streaming notes in appendix/FAQ
- Concurrency levels: 1, 8, 32? (needs to map to real app traffic)
  - Working direction: select 2–3 standardized levels; include “queueing visible at p95” notes
- Prompt set: finalize v3 “production mix” (prefill-heavy + balanced + decode-heavy) with clear distributions

4) Model shortlist (draft; subject to methodology + capacity)
Selection principles
- Popularity in production, mix of sizes, mix of architectures
- Must be stable and supported in Redwood catalog across target regions
- Avoid “weird one-off configs” for the headline story; prefer default-ish serving configs

Working model shortlist (names are placeholders until final catalog confirmation)
Tier A (must-have if supported)
- Llama 3.x 8B Instruct
- Llama 3.x 70B Instruct
- Mixtral 8x7B Instruct (or current Mixtral MoE equivalent)
- Qwen2.x 7B Instruct
- Qwen2.x 72B Instruct

Tier B (nice-to-have / if time)
- Smaller “economy” model (3–4B class) for ultra-low-cost comparison
- Code-focused model (if we can defend prompt set fit)
- Reranker/embedding benchmarks (likely out of scope for this report; revisit for v2)

Notes
- Henry to confirm which models are “supported for publication” vs “experimental” in each region.
- Jonas/Claire to sanity-check that chosen models cover meaningful diversity without exploding matrix size.

5) Region shortlist (draft)
Selection principles
- Must reflect where customers actually deploy + where we can reserve capacity for repeatable runs
- Must avoid publishing regions with known transient capacity constraints unless we can repeat runs reliably

Working region shortlist
- North America
  - us-east (primary)
  - us-west (secondary)
- Europe
  - eu-west
  - eu-central (if capacity is stable; otherwise keep to eu-west only)
- APAC
  - ap-southeast
  - ap-northeast (conditional)

Open question
- If we can’t support full APAC matrix, do we publish fewer regions or fewer models? (trade-off to decide by end of Week 1)

6) Competitive references (alignment with Legal)
We will:
- Lead with Redwood results + methodology transparency.
- If we include competitor context, it must be:
  - clearly labeled as “contextual baseline”
  - apples-to-apples as much as feasible (same prompt set, concurrency, regions, cache policy) OR explicitly caveated
  - reviewed + approved by Legal with retained substantiation artifacts

We will not:
- Claim “X% faster than [competitor]” unless Legal signs off on exact phrasing + we can reproduce with retained run manifests.
- Use “best/fastest/cheapest” global superlatives.

7) Deliverables + owners (initial)
Benchmarking + data pipeline
- Methodology owner: Claire Dubois
- Harness + runner: Rina Kobayashi
- Metric normalization/latency-$: Nadia Rahman (loop in; not present today)
- Region sweeps + capacity coordination: Vanessa Ortiz (+ Harish Reddy)
- Stability/variance gates: Jonas Weber

Content + web
- Narrative/report + blog: Ethan Wallace
- Landing page copy + methodology summary: Wei Chen (loop in)
- Interactive table implementation: Felix Schneider
- Visual/UX + charts style: Alicia Perez

GTM + enablement
- Launch plan + messaging: Soojin Lee
- Sales/SE enablement kit: Markus Klein + Stephanie Nguyen (loop in) + Lukas Meyer (EMEA)
- Email + funnel: Ben Carter

Legal/security reviews
- Claims review: Michael Grant + Sofia Mendes
- Public artifacts security review: Naomi Feldman (loop in)

8) Timeline (rough, for planning)
Week 1 (Jun 3–Jun 7)
- Lock v1 methodology (or at minimum lock what must be decided before running)
- Confirm model/region matrix size + capacity feasibility
- Draft report outline (sections + required charts)

Weeks 2–4
- Run region sweeps (repeatability + variance checks)
- Data validation + reruns where needed
- Draft copy v0 (report + landing page)

Weeks 5–6
- Internal review cycles: Eng, Product, Sales, Legal, Security
- Implement interactive page + analytics events
- Finalize PDF layout plan

Week 7
- Final data freeze + export artifacts
- Final legal sign-off on claims/disclaimers
- Enablement distribution + rehearsal for webinar/demo

Week 8 (launch week)
- Publish landing page + PDF + blog
- Email + community/social + partner amplification
- Monitor page performance + adjust guardrails

9) Risks + mitigations (early)
- Methodology credibility risk (fairness/cherry-picking)
  - Mitigation: publish configs, prompt sets, cache policy; include stability notes; retain run manifests
- Region capacity volatility
  - Mitigation: capacity reservations for sweeps; rerun windows; define “region excluded” threshold w/ explicit wording
- Legal risk on comparative claims
  - Mitigation: conservative copy; early Legal involvement; keep claims tied to specific measured conditions
- Web reliability (launch traffic)
  - Mitigation: caching layer for benchmark JSON; CDN; rate limits; pre-warm

10) Open questions to resolve (with proposed owner)
1) Final label for the metric (“latency/$” vs “latency per dollar” vs “latency efficiency”)
   - Owner: Soojin + Michael/Sofia (Legal)
2) Final caching/batching policy for headline numbers
   - Owner: Claire + Jonas + Rina
3) Model + region publication criteria (“supported” vs “experimental”)
   - Owner: Henry + Vanessa
4) Whether we include competitor baselines in v1
   - Owner: Soojin + Michael/Sofia + Jonas
5) What exactly goes into the interactive table v1 (filters + export)
   - Owner: Felix + Alicia + Ben

11) Action items (next 72 hours)
- Claire: circulate v1 methodology decision doc + list of unresolved items by EOD Jun 5
- Vanessa: confirm preliminary capacity reservation feasibility for target regions by Jun 5
- Henry: provide “supported for publication” model list per region (or draft) by Jun 6
- Ethan: draft report outline v0 (headings + required charts) by Jun 6
- Soojin: draft message house v0 + disallowed claims list; schedule Legal review block by Jun 6
- Felix/Ben: propose analytics event names for interactive page (filters/export/CTA) by Jun 6

Appendix (parking lot)
- Consider a short “How to reproduce” appendix for prospects (PoC-oriented), with explicit caveats.
- Consider an addendum plan for “model refresh cadence” post-launch (define what is ‘material’ and triggers v1.1).
